h1:
Uthai Thani Food
Sakae Krang Fish, Vietnamese Kuay Jub & Treats
intro: Uthai Thani is a riverside town on the Sakae Krang where you can eat freshwater fish at nearly every meal. The star is Sakae Krang giant gourami, which holds a Geographical Indication (GI) tag — firm meat with no muddy taste. Beyond that you'll find Vietnamese-style kuay jub, decades-old noodle shops, and souvenirs like pandan custard buns that everyone passing through stops for. We've rounded up the spots locals actually eat at.

blocks.html: Uthai Thani is a small town that punches above its weight at the table. The town sits along the Sakae Krang River, with a riverside morning market, noodle shops that have been open for decades, and river-fish restaurants scattered around Ko Thepho and along the water. If you like something a little different, there's Vietnamese kuay jub to try. We've sorted everything into sections — river fish, noodles, morning-market eats, and souvenirs — so it's easy to plan your eating around your trip.

blocks.text: Sakae Krang river fish — the town's signature

blocks.html: If you can only eat one thing in Uthai Thani, make it Sakae Krang giant gourami. It's raised in floating pens in the middle of the river where the current never stops, so the meat is firm and springy with none of the muddy taste you get from pond fish. The classic dishes are fried gourami with garlic, salt-grilled gourami, and gourami steamed with lime. Besides gourami you'll also find redtail catfish, sheatfish, butterfish, and clown knifefish depending on the season. Most river-fish places sit on the water or on floating rafts, and the atmosphere is especially nice toward evening.

items: Garlic-fried / fish-sauce-fried gourami — the most-ordered dish, firm flesh with crispy skin
Salt-grilled gourami — grilled whole and served hot with seafood dip, full fish flavor
Gourami steamed with lime — sour, spicy and fresh, good if you want something lighter
Redtail catfish tom yum / sheatfish jungle curry — hot, punchy soups that pair well with freshwater fish
Three-flavor fried butterfish — sweet, sour and spicy, found at the riverside rafts around Ko Thepho

blocks.title: Tips for ordering gourami
blocks.html: A big gourami can be turned into several dishes, so if there are only a few of you, ask the shop to split one fish two ways — half garlic-fried, half steamed with lime — and you'll get to try more in one meal. Riverside spots get busy on weekend evenings, so calling ahead to reserve a waterside table is the safer bet.

blocks.text: Fish and food spots locals actually go to

blocks.html: Picked from places with steady, real reviews on Wongnai and from word of mouth among locals — a mix of river-fish restaurants, noodle shops, and in-town spots, ordered so you can work through them easily. Prices are rough ranges and may shift with fish size and seasonal menus.

items.name: Pa Samran (Ko Thepho)
items.blurb: A river-fish restaurant on Ko Thepho along the Sakae Krang that locals think of first. Known for salt-grilled gourami, fish-sauce-fried gourami, steamed fish curry (ho mok), and braised fresh fish in soy. Lovely waterside seating toward evening. Open roughly 10:00–19:00.
items.meta: Ko Thepho, along the Sakae Krang · late morning to evening

items.name: Suan Ahan Nok Noi
items.blurb: A long-running Thai restaurant across from the provincial hall in town, with a wide menu. Strong on river-fish dishes, redtail catfish tom yum, and sea bass stir-fried with Chinese celery. Good for groups or families. Open roughly 10:00–20:00.
items.meta: Si Uthai Road, opposite the provincial hall · in town

items.name: Sala Coke Restaurant
items.blurb: A spot on the road toward Tha Kham, known for garlic-fried gourami and sheatfish jungle curry — punchy, homestyle flavors. Open long hours, 09:00–21:00, so you can drop by at lunch or dinner.
items.meta: On the road to Tha Kham · open all day

items.name: Je Da Pla Luak
items.blurb: An evening rice-soup spot in the Tha Chang Road area in town, known for fresh blanched fish with a spicy dip and stir-fried pak wan greens over high heat. Open afternoon to evening, around 15:00–21:00 — an easygoing dinner for townsfolk.
items.meta: Tha Chang Road, Mueang district · dinner

items.name: Kuay Tiao Ton Yang
items.blurb: An old-school noodle shop in the Nam Sueam area, known for stewed beef and marinated pork noodles in a sweet, bone-stock broth topped with crispy pork rinds. Open 09:00–15:30, closed Sundays — it's popular and often sells out before afternoon.
items.meta: Nam Sueam, Mueang district · morning to afternoon (closed Sun)

items.name: Je Nok Chicken Noodles
items.blurb: Chicken noodles in the Rak Uthit Road area, open for over 40 years. Clear, sweet chicken-bone broth that's easy to eat at any age. Open roughly 09:30–15:00 — a breakfast-to-lunch staple for locals.
items.meta: Rak Uthit Road · morning to afternoon

items.name: Je Nguang Kuay Jub (Thap Than)
items.blurb: A clear-broth kuay jub shop in Thap Than district that locals talk about a lot. Soft noodle rolls, clean offal, and a bone broth fragrant with white pepper. People heading toward Thap Than tend to stop in — cheap and filling.
items.meta: Thap Than district · clear-broth kuay jub

items.name: Thung Noen Jaeng Cafe & Resort
items.blurb: A spot set out in the fields in the Noen Jaeng area, photogenic and relaxed. The standout is steamed snakehead fish (paesa) alongside light Thai dishes — good for a late-morning or afternoon sit-down. Open roughly 10:00–22:00.
items.meta: Noen Jaeng · cafe in the fields

blocks.text: Vietnamese kuay jub and noodle dishes

blocks.html: Beyond the old-school noodle shops, Uthai Thani also has Vietnamese-style kuay jub to try — round flour rolls in a clear broth fragrant with white pepper, served with minced pork, a poached egg, and Vietnamese-style offal. It's not heavily spiced and goes down easy. Some shops in town and in the districts sell it as a breakfast-to-late-morning meal, around ฿40–60 a bowl. To be straight with you, the most famous original Vietnamese kuay jub is over in Ubon Ratchathani, but Uthai Thani has shops that do it well if you want a change of pace from regular noodles.

items: Vietnamese kuay jub — round flour rolls in clear broth, minced pork, poached egg, pork offal, topped with fragrant white pepper
Clear-broth kuay jub (Je Nguang, Thap Than) — soft rolls, clean offal, sweet bone broth
Stewed beef / marinated pork noodles — the traditional style; Ton Yang is the spot for this
Chicken noodles — clear broth sweet with chicken bones; Je Nok has been open over 40 years

blocks.title: Noodle shops open early
blocks.html: Many of the old-school noodle and kuay jub shops open in the morning and run to the afternoon, and they sell out before closing. If you're after a famous shop, plan your meal for the late morning to be safe — don't leave it until evening, because plenty of them will already be closed.

blocks.text: The Sakae Krang riverside morning market

blocks.html: The morning market along the Sakae Krang in town is where you'll see Uthai Thani life at its clearest — fresh fish, local vegetables, breakfast foods, and old-style sweets laid out all along the waterfront. Locals come here to do their shopping and eat breakfast. The atmosphere is simple but full of charm, and you can graze your way through a lot of things in one place.

items: Fresh gourami & freshwater fish — fish stalls straight from the Sakae Krang; take it home or have a shop cook it
Noodles & gourami tom yum — a punchy breakfast made with fish fresh from the market
Old-style sweets & breakfast eats — traditional Thai sweets and hot fried snacks at the stalls
Dried goods & sun-dried fish — easy to buy as a souvenir to take home

blocks.title: What time to hit the morning market
blocks.html: The riverside morning market is liveliest around 6:00–8:00, when everything's still fresh and the breakfast options are all out. Go late and some things may be sold out. Get up a little early, then keep strolling along the river afterward — you'll get both the food and the early-morning atmosphere.

Uthai Thani souvenirs range from popular sweets to local goods — pick based on who they're for and how far you're traveling. The one nearly everyone passing through stops for is the pandan custard bun, while for dried goods there's sun-dried fish made from river fish.

items.name: Mae Puay Lang custard buns
items.blurb: The town's famous custard-bun shop. Soft buns with fragrant pandan custard filling — the souvenir people passing through Uthai Thani always stop to buy.

items.name: Sun-dried fish
items.blurb: Fresh freshwater fish salted and dried in the sun for a day — firm and fragrant, just the right saltiness once fried, keeps well, and easy to carry home.

items.name: Lao Khrang woven textiles
items.blurb: Local handwoven cloth with naga and hook patterns, rooted in traditional craft — a good keepsake souvenir to take along.

items.name: Local goods at Sao Hai Market
items.blurb: A community-style market in Ban Rai with organic vegetables, old-fashioned sweets, foraged goods, and crafts. Open only Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays, 09:00–16:00.

blocks.text: Planning a full day of eating in Uthai Thani

blocks.html: If you've only got one day, it comes together easily — start at the riverside morning market, follow with an old-school noodle shop, then close out with a river-fish meal along the Sakae Krang in the evening. Here's a meal-by-meal eating guide to follow.

items.activity: Walk the Sakae Krang riverside morning market; try noodles or gourami tom yum
items.note: Go before 8am while everything's still fresh and catch the riverside atmosphere

items.activity: Stop at an old-school noodle shop — Kuay Tiao Ton Yang or Je Nok chicken noodles
items.note: The famous shops sell out before afternoon, so late morning is safest

items.activity: Buy Mae Puay Lang custard buns as a souvenir, or sit at Thung Noen Jaeng cafe
items.note: On weekends you can add a stop at Sao Hai Market in Ban Rai

items.activity: Close out with a river-fish meal along the Sakae Krang at Pa Samran, Ko Thepho
items.note: Order salt-grilled gourami and the steamed-lime version, and sit by the water for the cool breeze

faq.q: What food should you try in Uthai Thani?
faq.a: Sakae Krang giant gourami is the number one thing people think of — a pen-raised freshwater fish with firm meat and no muddy taste, done garlic-fried, salt-grilled, or steamed with lime. After that come Vietnamese kuay jub, old-school noodle shops, and souvenirs like pandan custard buns.

faq.q: Where's a good place to eat Sakae Krang gourami?
faq.a: The most talked-about spots are Pa Samran on Ko Thepho along the Sakae Krang, Suan Ahan Nok Noi across from the provincial hall in town, and Sala Coke on the road toward Tha Kham. All three are strong on river-fish dishes — it's worth calling to reserve a waterside table on weekend evenings.

faq.q: Is the Vietnamese kuay jub in Uthai Thani the original?
faq.a: To be straight with you, the most famous original Vietnamese kuay jub is over in Ubon Ratchathani, but Uthai Thani does have shops that make kuay jub well — like Je Nguang in Thap Than district, a clear-broth version with soft rolls and clean offal. It's worth a try for a change of pace from regular noodles.

faq.q: What souvenirs does Uthai Thani have?
faq.a: The souvenirs people buy most often are custard buns from a famous shop like Mae Puay Lang, sun-dried fish made from river fish, and Lao Khrang handwoven textiles in local patterns. If you come on a weekend, stop by Sao Hai Market in Ban Rai for more local goods and crafts.

faq.q: What time does the Sakae Krang riverside morning market open?
faq.a: The Sakae Krang riverside morning market is liveliest around 6:00–8:00, with fresh fish, local vegetables, breakfast foods, and old-style sweets. Go late and some things may be sold out — get up a little early to catch both the food and the riverside morning atmosphere.
